This game got a lot of hate at launch (for good reason) and honestly most of what you’ve probably already heard about it is true. It plays like a bad clone of Far Cry. Basically every cutscene is just a slideshow, some without any spoken words. The gunplay is serviceable but noticeably clunky. The AI is very stupid, even on higher difficulties. This is probably the most aggressively average game on the market. That all said, I’ve been having a really good time playing cross-platform co-op with my girlfriend who does not play games nearly as often as I do. There are no issues with connectivity and the game has yet to crash. There are some cosmetic DLCs, but no predatory micro-transactions whatsoever. You can unlock a lot of cosmetics just by playing the game. If you’re the type of person that can enjoy  a 5/10, pick this one up when it’s on sale. It’s well worth the $20 I spent.

Note: when you first boot up the game it will overlay a server connection thing over the EULA you have to sign. if you spam enter, you can get it to work. if you do not do this, it will never connect. 

So all in all I followed red fall for a bit when it came out because I liked the prey and death loop games. ultimately I didn't get it until more recently on sale and I think that was a good choice. I have actually been rather enjoying it. that said I understand why it did not do so well even after updates. the story is a little convoluted and kind of sucks, loot variety is a bit limited, and it was originally focused as a multiplayer only experience. signal player isn't too bad, but some of the mechanics are still intended for multi. I also wish I was able to make a character rather then choose one, but the fact that is has custom dialog is cool. some of the abilities don't make a lot of scenes but then again we are dealing with vampires (possibly from another dimension?). 
The game was also delayed a number of times, partly due to the pandemic, and during that time other more well known titles came out during that time that made this not as interesting. 
I do actually like the gameplay a bit, even with its flaws. its like far cry with a L4D approach to mobs (that do not work well with single player. think smoker, but vampire). it still has some odd quarks, but I think a bunch of things have been ironed out in the last patch they did. the AI still is not super grate, and I have clipped into some stuff, but I am enjoying exploring the map and looking for collectables. the added story bits they give are cool, even if its is a little too edgy for me at times. 
I think red fall is also meant to be like Salem or other towns like it here in MA, so that is cool. if you look at the museums they also use some of the props from Dishonored and death loop... probably not the same timeline but still cool to see. 

also customization exists but is limited. some of it is found, some of it is static on map. there are a lot more gun skins and stake types then character skins, with like 4-5 skins being various wolf fur suit costumes denoting difficulty clears. 
I'm also not sure why a first responder trained in disaster relief made a robot with a shotgun or carries C4... but if you don't think about it too hard its fun.

after playing it for a bit- I can say that the fun part about the game is the fact that it has a lot of little collectables and little secrets, with the added benefit of having skills that point them out on the map. the vampire nests that it generates are also pretty cool and makes for a more dynamic map difficulty, but the mechanics is based around multiplayer and the timer both for looting at the end and the mechanics of the boss fight can be frustrating if you are going in solo. I don't mean because its difficult, I mean because once you win there is a time limit that you are very unlikely to be bale to loot all the reward chests from, and the bosses do attacks that prevent you from being able to attack/move/heal in anticipation of a team mate to save you. You need to either chunk damage and run, or stay far away to be safe. this attack will also interrupt and dismiss the healing class ability, meaning that it is semi useless outside of its initial healing burst and side effects. the healing skill in general is just very lackluster, and if the class did not have throwable C4 and a robot, id probably have switched off to the grate value borderlands sniper class.
The game that buried Arkane. Redfall isn't bad by any means... it's just not very good either.

I know this flopped hard on release but I am really enjoying it, I'd give it a 7/10 for the $20 I paid for it. Technical issues are not present for me, it runs smoothly and doesn't crash. Gameplay-wise this feels like the shooting mechanics from Deathloop were jumbled around into a fairly basic looter-shooter, nothing incredible but far from terrible. Arkane's talents were not suited for such a game, their sharp art direction and intricate level design stand out as always, it's just that the game is basically a mid-tier Far Cry clone. Arkane went this direction instead of sticking with their tried and tested im-sim/stealth mechanics, I'm sure purely at the direction from their parent company scrambling for a big multiplayer live service hit, and unfortunately this didn't move the needle for Microsoft so the studio was axed.

This game is basically Homefront: The Revolution with an injection of Arkane's stylishness, the world is beautifully detailed, the gunplay is slick, the lore is interesting, but prettymuch everything else (storyline, main characters, RPG mechanics, open world design, loot system) is very mid. If you can enjoy truly mid games (like Homefront or Far Cry: New Dawn), or are a die-hard Arkane fan (like myself), you may enjoy a solo playthrough. Buy for $20 or less with low expectations, you may be pleasantly surprised.

It's an absolute mystery to me why this game wasn't a success. I guess that when it first came out it must have had more bugs or performance issues, and I'm sure a number of people were pissed about how much simpler it is than other games from this studio. But coming to it a couple years after the rest of the world forgot about it, I think it's one of my favorite looter-shooter games of all time. It pairs the gameplay of Borderlands with the vibes of Silent Hill, which, come on. It's hard to top that combo. 

This game does the same thing a number of other games do, like Dead Island or Dying Light or Far Cry, but with one crucial difference, which is that there is ABSOLUTELY NO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. So often I get into an open world shooter like this and find myself losing endless time to things that are neither looting nor shooting: long, dull cutscenes; unnecessary travel time across unnecessarily oversized and empty maps; horribly designed mini-games and side activities. None of it is ever fun, just terrible padding. This game does not have that problem. You explore, you shoot, and you loot. And it's very good at all of those things. 

The hallmarks of Arkane are definitely still here. You can approach fights strategically, using positioning and environmental hazards. World building and design are absolutely top notch (I will say there's significantly less story than in something like Dishonored or Prey, but what there is is very well done, I think). It doesn't have those games' sophistication in terms of player choice, but it doesn't need to, because it's just not an immersive sim. 

It's not without its flaws, of course. Leveling happens too slowly and your choices of where to place skill points are often not very interesting. (Although to mitigate that there is a second, reputation-based progression system that does have some very helpful abilities in it.) There's a very small range of weapon types that aren't substantially different from one another. Story, like I said, is minimal. But honestly, if you like something like Borderlands and don't go in expecting something extremely complex or lengthy, this is ultimate video game comfort food. I'd have a hard time recommending it any more highly.
